summary: Intermittent model artifact fetch failures from private deploy due to split-horizon DNS + TGW route propagation race causing OCSP lookup mismatch
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent failures fetching model artifacts from S3/HTTP origin during private deployment. Failures correlate with NAT/TGW route churn and control-plane DNS conditional forwarding. Impact: model pulls fail sporadically causing cold-start timeouts and 5xx for in-flight requests. Environment: private deployment in Acme AI VPC connected to Redwood control plane via Transit Gateway and a pair of NAT gateways in the egress subnet.

Observed behaviour: when upstream route propagation completes, DNS results from split-horizon forwarder flip between an internal resolver (that rewrites OCSP responders to private IPs) and public resolution. At the same time ephemeral egress IPs are reassigned during NAT replacement, producing transient TLS stapling verification failures and OCSP timeouts, which our artifact fetch code treats as fatal rather than retryable.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run a private deployment with VPC attached to TGW and an internal conditional DNS forwarder that rewrites ocsp.example.com to a private probe IP.
2) Trigger NAT gateway replacement (scale down/up or AWS-managed maintenance) or update TGW route table to simulate propagation delay.
3) Immediately attempt model artifact pull for a new model version or scale up a serving pod to force cold-start fetch.
4) Observe intermittent TLS handshake failures and OCSP lookup timeouts in the serving runtime logs; artifact fetch fails after single attempt.
logs: [2026-03-10T14:03:12Z] artifact-fetcher WARN fetch failed: tls: failed to verify certificate: stapled OCSP response invalid (lookup timeout)
[2026-03-10T14:03:12Z] egress INFO nat-replace detected old-eip 54.12.23.45 -> new-eip 18.234.8.101; route-propagation delta=18s
[2026-03-10T14:03:14Z] tls DEBUG handshake failed with s3-presigned.example.net: remote error: tls: handshake failure
investigation_notes: Initial triage: failures coincide with NAT replacement events and TGW route updates recorded in the customer's cloud console.
DNS traces show split-horizon forwarder returning private OCSP IPs for some queries and public IPs for others within a 10-30s window — indicates race between resolver cache and TGW route propagation.
OCSP responder IP flip leads to connection attempts that exit different egress paths; some IPs are reachable only via updated TGW routes and others time out when attempted over the old path.
Artifact fetch stack treats OCSP lookup as blocking step and does not perform backoff + fallback to control-plane proxy; single failure results in request abort.
comments: Priya Natarajan (Support): Customer reports spike of artifact fetch errors between 14:00-14:10 UTC. Affects cold starts only. Asked for packet captures and resolv.conf from affected host.
Acme AI (Jake Alvarez): Provided tcpdump and VPC flow logs. Noted that maintenance window correlates with AWS-managed NAT replacement. Willing to test quick fix (persistent EIP) in dev account.
Mei Lin (SRE): Confirmed TGW route propagation logs show delay ~15-25s on propagation to transit attachments. Split-horizon forwarder TTL is 30s which can present mixed answers during that window.

Carlos Mendes (Assignee): Reproduced locally in staging using TGW route change simulation and patched artifact-fetcher to retry OCSP lookup and fall back to control-plane proxy for up to 6s; initial results show retries reduce failure rate.
hypothesis: Race condition between split-horizon DNS forwarder TTL and TGW route propagation causes some OCSP queries to resolve to IPs not yet reachable from the current egress path.
When OCSP connection attempts fail, TLS stapling validation aborts and the artifact fetcher does not retry or switch egress path, resulting in artifact pull failure.
temporary_workaround: Customer applied a short-term mitigation: pinned NAT egress to a small pool of persistent EIPs and increased DNS forwarder TTL to 120s. They also enabled the Redwood control-plane egress-proxy for artifact fetches. This reduced the incidence to near-zero during testing.
proposed_fix: Engineering will implement two changes: 1) make artifact fetcher tolerant to OCSP transient failures by retrying OCSP lookups with exponential backoff and falling back to control-plane proxy; 2) add diagnostics to detect mixed split-horizon answers and surface a warning in the console with recommended TTL/route-propagation guardrails.
resolution: In progress - partial mitigation applied by customer (persistent EIP pool + control-plane proxy). Engineering patch PR #1298 adds retry/fallback behavior; currently in review and staging testing. Plan is to complete rollout to hosted agent image and provide config guidance to customer. Follow-up: SRE to coordinate with Acme AI on permanent route/TTL tuning and to add a runbook entry for NAT replacement windows.
rollout_notes: Target rollout: canary to 5% of private-deploy fleets after PR merged, monitor artifact-fetch error rates and TLS handshake failure counts for 48 hours. Notify Acme AI prior to canary and schedule full rollout during low-traffic window.
